function: Jointly learns AP transmit/receive mode, user association, ISAC precoding and multi-target position and velocity estimation from echoes, under a communication sum-rate constraint (p. 5).
system: Cell-free ISAC: 14 Tx-APs and 2 Rx-APs with 8-antenna ULAs, 16 single-antenna users, 3 targets, OFDM with 32 subcarriers, 24 GHz, 120 MHz; no RIS (p. 12).
method: Heterogeneous GAT: dynamic framework (structural and temporal attention, 3D-CNN) and lightweight mirror-GAT; supervised offline training with estimation MSE plus sum-rate penalty, 3D-CNN pre-trained (p. 8-9).
data_channel: Synthetic: 12,000 simulated samples; channel not specified beyond LoS path loss (exponent 2.1-3.8), Rayleigh/Rician implied; Sionna-RT ray tracing only in a robustness test (p. 4, 12, 15).
test_conditions: Default setup 14 Tx-APs, 2 Rx-APs, 8 antennas, 16 users, 3 targets; tests vary antennas (4-12), symbols (8-24), Sionna-RT, noisy CSI; paper says tests differ from training (p. 12-15).
baselines: Heuristic+GAT, Random+GAT (own GAT with heuristic or random association), MMSE+CNN [21] (3D-CNN estimator), ZF+FFT [40], two-stage maximum-likelihood [41] (p. 13).
metrics: Position RMSE (m), velocity RMSE (m/s), achievable sum-rate (bps/Hz); parameter count, execution time and backhaul signaling values (p. 4-5, 13-15).
complexity: Number of parameters and average execution time versus antenna count for both frameworks (Fig. 13); backhaul signaling counted in values exchanged; no FLOPs or big-O order (p. 9, 15).
q1_support: p. 12: "the path-loss exponent is uniformly distributed between 2.1 and 3.8"
q2_support: p. 13: "achieving excellent estimation performance even under testing configurations that differ from those used during training"
q3_support: p. 13: "using a centralized 3D-CNN model for signal-level fusion"; p. 13: "the classical 3D-FFT method"
q4_support: p. 15: "in terms of model size (number of parameters) and average execution time"
notes: Included, area 5: the learned networks choose AP mode, user association and precoding that serve communication and sensing and also estimate target position and velocity, so the work passes above_phy through the learned precoding (p. 5, 8); an earlier conference version was a positioning-only paper (p. 1; ref. [1] on p. 16). q1=0: the main channel is a custom synthetic model (path-loss exponent 2.1-3.8 on p. 12, 'conventional Rayleigh and Rician' implied on p. 15); Sionna-RT ray tracing appears only in the practical analysis (p. 14-15, Table III) and the paper does not say the models were trained on it, reviewer may confirm. q2=1 rests on the explicit statement on p. 13; the paper does not detail which antenna counts or symbol counts were used in training. q3=1: learned baseline MMSE+CNN [21] (3D-CNN), classical baselines ZF+FFT [40] and two-stage maximum-likelihood [41], all compared on position and velocity RMSE (Figs. 6-8, p. 13-14); Heuristic+GAT and Random+GAT are variants of the proposed frameworks and not counted. q4: parameters and execution time (Fig. 13, p. 15). q5: synthetic data generated by the authors, no link or DOI to code or data; the only URL (p. 17) is an author homepage.
